put.summary: Pick up, assign, reassign or unassign a submitted assessment request (human Security Analyst only)
put.description: The only writer of a request's assignment. The caller names the new analyst (an IdamBox User documentId, or null to unassign) and the assignee they last saw; the server derives the action (pick-up, assign, reassign or unassign) and, under the request lock, refuses a request the caller raised (403), a draft, an assignee who changed since the caller saw it, an ineligible target and the unassignment of a released request (409), each with its closed reason. Naming the current assignee changes nothing and records nothing.

get.description: Exactly the people the assignment operation would accept as the request's assignee: active human Security Analysts, never the Security Analyst Agent, an inactive user or the request's own requestor. People are a documentId and a display name only, ordered by display name, at most 50, searchable by name with q. The current assignee is listed. A Security Analyst who raised the request is refused with 403 OWN_REQUEST, and a draft with 409 REQUEST_NOT_SUBMITTED.

get.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, and a missing request, is answered 404 with the same message. A page holds the newest notes before the before sequence (all notes when absent), at most limit (default 20, at most 50), returned oldest first; meta.hasEarlier says whether earlier notes exist. A note is unread for the caller when it was written in the other part, not by the caller, and above the caller's lastReadSequence. Listing never marks anything read. changesAiInputs is served to a human Security Analyst only.

post.summary: Add an attributed, append-only note to a submitted assessment request
post.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, and a missing request, is answered 404 with the same message. The body is plain text, trimmed, with CRLF and CR normalised to LF, 1 to 5,000 characters, no control character other than tab and newline. The server assigns the sequence (the request's highest plus one, under the request lock), the posting time and the author's part. A note can never be edited or deleted.

post.summary: Mark an assessment request's notes read through one note
post.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, a missing request and a note that is not on the request are answered 404. Under the request lock the caller's one read state for the request advances to the named note's sequence; it only ever increases, so naming an earlier note changes nothing and succeeds. The read state is the caller's own and is never shown to anyone else.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The opaque assessment request documentId

200.description: The caller's read state after the call

put.summary: Mark or unmark a note on an assessment request as changing the AI inputs
put.description: Human Security Analyst only (D-26, D-30): the Requestor, the Security Analyst Agent and every other caller are refused 403 before anything is read. An analyst who raised the request is refused 403 with the closed reason OWN_REQUEST (G-1). A missing request and a note that is not on the request are answered 404. Under the request lock the note is re-read; while the request accepts notes the mark is set to the given value and one event is appended to the note's AI-input history, in the same write. Setting the value the note already has succeeds and writes nothing; Undo is a second change. A request that takes no new note (released, closed or returned to draft) answers 409 NOTES_CLOSED, and a note whose history is full (200 events) or cannot be read answers 409 HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE, with nothing written. The mark chooses inputs only; it never generates, accepts or releases anything.

parameters.description: The opaque documentId of a note on the request

200.description: The note after the call, as a Security Analyst sees it

get.summary: List an assessment request's files, newest first, with whether the caller may add one
get.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, and a missing request, is answered 404 with the same message. Lists every file of the request, removed and blocked ones included, newest first, at most 60 (the lifetime bound). Each file names its uploader by display name and part, its upload time, the note it came with, its state and the actions the caller may take now. meta.add says whether the caller may add a file now, with the closed reason when not, whether a note is needed, what remains of the limits, the limits and the allowed types. No storage address, digest or extracted text is served. Listing writes nothing.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The opaque assessment request documentId

200.description: The request's files and the caller's add facts

post.summary: Add one file to an assessment request
post.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, and a missing request, is answered 404 with the same message. Multipart with exactly one file part and an optional noteId part; any other part is 400 with nothing written. On a draft only its requestor adds, with no note (an analyst is refused 409 REQUEST_NOT_SUBMITTED; a noteId is refused 409 ATTACHMENT_NOTE_INVALID). After submission, until release or closure, the requestor and any human Security Analyst add, each file with the caller's own note on the same request posted within the last 60 minutes (409 ATTACHMENT_NOTE_REQUIRED without one, ATTACHMENT_NOTE_INVALID for any other). A released or closed request takes none (409 ATTACHMENTS_CLOSED). The file is checked by its content and extension against PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, TXT, PNG and JPEG (415). A DOCX, XLSX or PPTX packaged in a way CSRM will not read (an archive comment, more than 10,000 parts, more than 1 GiB declared, a part declaring more than 200 times its compressed size, ZIP64, or a compression method other than stored or deflate) is refused 415 ATTACHMENT_UNSUPPORTED_STRUCTURE, and one carrying active content beyond macros (an external linked object, template, frame or subdocument, or an ActiveX control) 415 ATTACHMENT_ACTIVE_CONTENT. The file must hold 1 to 26,214,400 bytes (400 ATTACHMENT_EMPTY, 413 ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE) and is scanned for malware (422 ATTACHMENT_MALWARE_FOUND with details.detection). At most 20 active and 60 stored files per request, counted under the request lock (409 ATTACHMENT_LIMIT_REACHED, ATTACHMENT_LIFETIME_LIMIT_REACHED). While the file checks are busy, the upload is refused at once with 503 ATTACHMENT_BUSY and may be retried. Nothing of a refused file is kept. A file the scanner cannot check is stored in quarantine with state pending and cannot be downloaded until a scan passes.

get.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, a missing request and a file id that is not on this request are answered 404 with the same message. Only a clean file that has not been removed is sent. A reader asking for any other file is answered 409 with its closed reason: ATTACHMENT_QUARANTINED while it waits for its malware check, ATTACHMENT_BLOCKED after the check found malware, ATTACHMENT_REMOVED after its removal, and ATTACHMENT_UNAVAILABLE when its stored bytes are gone. Strapi reads the stored bytes and checks them against the SHA-256 recorded at upload before sending any; bytes that no longer match are refused with ATTACHMENT_INTEGRITY_FAILED and recorded as a security event. The file is sent as an attachment under its recorded type's media type, never inline, never cached and sandboxed. Each download is recorded as a security event.

put.summary: Remove one of an assessment request's files, or restore it
put.description: Reachable by the request's requestor and any human Security Analyst; anyone else, a missing request and a file id that is not on this request are answered 404 with the same message. The body is exactly { data: { removed } }; any other key is 400. removed true removes the file softly: it records who removed it and when, takes it out of the main list and out of downloads, and ends its AI inclusion, deleting its stored text; its bytes are kept, and the record follows the request's retention. removed false restores it, recorded as an event; a restore never includes it in the AI inputs again. No reason or confirmation is asked. The uploader removes their own files; any human Security Analyst who did not raise the request removes any file from submission until release or closure; anyone else is refused 403 NOT_UPLOADER. Only the person who removed a file restores it (403 NOT_REMOVER). On a draft only its requestor acts (409 REQUEST_NOT_SUBMITTED); a released or closed request is read-only (409 ATTACHMENTS_CLOSED). A blocked file is never restored (409 ATTACHMENT_BLOCKED), a restore that would make a 21st active file is refused (409 ATTACHMENT_LIMIT_REACHED), and a file whose history is full or unreadable is not changed (409 HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE). Removing a removed file, or restoring one that is not removed, changes nothing and answers the file as it is. Every removal and restore is recorded as a security event.

put.summary: Include one of an assessment request's files in what the AI may read, or exclude it
put.description: Human Security Analyst only (D-30, D-38): the Requestor, the Security Analyst Agent and every other caller are refused 403 before anything is read. An analyst who raised the request is refused 403 with the closed reason OWN_REQUEST (G-1). A missing request and a file id that is not on this request are answered 404. The body is exactly { data: { included } }; any other key is 400. Inclusion is off by default. Including a file extracts its text in a bounded worker, outside the request lock, and stores at most 20,000 characters with the characters available, the characters kept, whether the text was cut, the extractor's version and when it ran; excluding deletes the stored text and its facts. Each change is appended to the file's history and recorded as a security event, never with the text or the file's name. A change is accepted only from submission until release or closure: 409 REQUEST_NOT_SUBMITTED on a draft and 409 ATTACHMENTS_CLOSED on a released or closed request. Excluding is always allowed while the request takes changes. Including needs a clean file that has not been removed and carries text (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV or TXT): 409 ATTACHMENT_REMOVED, ATTACHMENT_BLOCKED, ATTACHMENT_QUARANTINED, ATTACHMENT_UNAVAILABLE or ATTACHMENT_NOT_TEXT_BEARING otherwise; stored bytes that no longer match their digest are 409 ATTACHMENT_INTEGRITY_FAILED, and a file with no text the extractor can read is 409 ATTACHMENT_TEXT_UNAVAILABLE. Including is refused while the request's AI data policy refuses, so the inclusion never promises what generation would refuse: 409 AI_CLASSIFICATION_ABOVE_CEILING or AI_POLICY_NOT_CONFIGURED. Setting the value the file already has changes nothing, and a file whose history is full or unreadable is not changed (409 HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE). While text extraction is busy, an inclusion is refused at once with 503 ATTACHMENT_BUSY and may be retried; nothing is changed. The inclusion chooses inputs only; it never generates, accepts or releases anything.

The released risk assessment exactly as its released reads disclose it, read through the one released-assessment record-read check: XLSX holds a Summary sheet (the assessment and request numbers, the request title, the Released date and who released it, the overall rating and control effectiveness, the summary, the overall rationale, the recommendations and the next review date), a Risks sheet (one row per Risk the released risks read returns, so no withdrawn Risk) and a Mitigation controls sheet (one row per control implementation of those Risks, keyed by risk number), then an About this export sheet that carries the AI assistance notice when AI assisted; CSV holds the Risks or the Mitigation controls table the table parameter names. The export takes no columns parameter (UI-D5). A Requestor exports only a released assessment of a request they raised: another person's, or their own unreleased one, is the missing record's 404. A Security Analyst exports any released assessment, with the same tables a Requestor gets; an unreleased one is 409 ASSESSMENT_NOT_RELEASED. It needs GET /api/v1/risk_assessments/{assessmentId} as well, and the service identity is refused whatever it holds. Each admitted attempt is recorded as one security event naming the exporter, the view (released-assessment), the assessment, the format, the table and the row count, never a cell value.

post.description: Human Security Analyst only (Phase 16 D-05, D-06, D-09, D-11, D-43). Withdraws the named Risks of one unreleased assessment in one transaction under the assessment's editable guard: each Risk that is active gets withdrawnAt, withdrawnBy and withdrawalReason and one `withdrawn` history row, and keeps its number, fields, control implementations and AI provenance. An already withdrawn Risk is reported in `unchanged` with no history row. `{ riskIds, reason }` records the typed reason; `{ riskIds, undo: true }` restores the reason the Risk held before its reinstatement (400 when it has none) and marks the history row as an Undo. A Risk that does not exist or belongs to another assessment refuses the whole batch with 404. A batch that withdraws something takes the accepted-edit transition (a release-ready in-review assessment returns to draft); one that withdraws nothing changes nothing. A released or otherwise not editable assessment is 409 ASSESSMENT_NOT_MUTABLE.

get.summary: Read a risk assessment's AI proposals, their runs and states, and what the analyst may do now (human Security Analyst only)
get.description: Phase 16 D-41. The open items first, grouped by run newest first, then the 50 most recently decided items, with each run's facts, each item's state folded from its decision events, staleness for an open change, similarity, sources, decision facts, the derived open count and per-risk open counts, the viewer's actions, and the active and recently failed jobs. Nothing beyond the immutable proposal and its append-only decisions is stored. Refused with 403 OWN_REQUEST to an analyst who raised the request.

parameters.name: assessmentId
parameters.description: The Strapi documentId of the risk assessment

get.summary: Compute one analyst report from current records
get.description: Each report is computed on read from existing records inside the Security Analyst's Risk Register and review scopes; nothing is stored and no report widens that scope. Every Risk figure counts open Risks, those with no closure date. risk-exposure counts released open Risks and, apart, the open Risks still under assessment; treatment-performance and control-effectiveness count open Risks in both stages. Only assessment-throughput takes a query parameter, period; a period on any other report, or any other query key, is rejected with 400. A key that names no report answers 404. Human Security Analyst only.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: assessment-throughput only: the calendar months, ending with the current UTC month, that the release figures cover. Absent means 6.

200.description: One computed report, discriminated by its key

post.summary: Export one analyst report's tables as an XLSX workbook or one table as a CSV file (human Security Analyst only)
post.description: Phase 19 (D-03, D-13, D-16 to D-18, D-22; UI-D5). The report is computed exactly as GET /api/v1/reports/{reportKey} computes it, with the report's own query parser, figures and windows, and shaped as the tables its page shows. XLSX holds one sheet per report table, in page order, then an About this export sheet with the report's As at date and, for assessment-throughput, its Period; CSV holds the one table the body names. A report export takes no columns (UI-D5). Only a human Security Analyst holding the export, GET /api/v1/reports/{reportKey} and the analyst insight scope's underlying reads may export; the service identity is refused whatever it holds. Each admitted attempt is recorded as one security event naming the exporter, the view (report:{reportKey}), the format, the table and the row count, never a cell value.

format.description: The file format: xlsx (a workbook of the report's tables and an About this export sheet) or csv (UTF-8 with a BOM, the one table named by table).

table.description: One of the report's table keys (risk-exposure: ratings, residual-by-treatment-status, exposed-systems, under-assessment; treatment-performance: due-state, treatment-status; assessment-throughput: released-per-month, request-lifecycle; control-effectiveness: implementation-status, effectiveness-rating). Required when format is csv; refused (400) when format is xlsx.

timeZone.description: The viewer's IANA time zone, used for the file name's local date and the exported-at time. Absent: UTC, noted in the file. A zone the server does not know is a 400.

query.description: The report's own query parameters as strings, parsed by the report's own parser: only assessment-throughput takes one, period ("6" or "12"; absent means 6). Any other key, or a value the report refuses, is a 400.

200.description: The report as a file download: its tables as display values (counts as numbers, ratings, statuses and months in the page's words), computed from the same figures the report read returns. A text value beginning with =, +, -, @, a tab or a line break starts with an apostrophe so it opens as text; an XLSX cell is always a typed value, never a formula.

Content-Disposition.description: attachment, with an ASCII filename and the RFC 5987 UTF-8 filename* of {reportKey}-report-{local date YYYY-MM-DD}.xlsx, or {reportKey}-{table slug}-{local date YYYY-MM-DD}.csv for one table

X-CSRM-Row-Count.description: The data rows the file holds

400.description: The export body is invalid: not a JSON object, a key other than format, table, timeZone and query (columns included), a missing or unknown format, a table missing for csv, given for xlsx or not one of the report's tables, an unknown time zone, or a query the report refuses. No reason is named.

403.description: The signed-in identity may not export the report: it is not a human Security Analyst holding the export, the report read and the insight scope's underlying reads, or it is an automation identity, which every export refuses

422.description: The export would hold more rows than one export may (EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT, with details.rowCount and details.rowCap); or EXPORT_CELL_TOO_LONG when format is xlsx and a text cell is longer than Excel's 32,767-character limit (with details.column and details.cellLimit), and the CSV holds the value whole. No file is written

scimSourceBearer.description: Identity Source bearer credential; independent of CSRM authentication.

RiskHistoryRelationValue.description: A related record as it was named when the change was recorded.

RiskHistoryValue.description: A recorded value: a scalar as stored, or a related record with its label at the time.

RiskHistoryControl.description: The control a control implementation event concerns.

RiskHistoryChanges.description: The change envelope v1. `control` is present only on the control implementation kinds; withdrawn and reinstated events list no fields.

recordedFrom.description: The earliest event's time, or null when the Risk has no history (History recorded from {date}).

RiskSuggestionsRequest.description: An optional instruction to the AI for Suggest more risks (Phase 16 D-27, Phase 15's bounds): at most 500 characters, no control or bidirectional characters, and not a repeat of the Requestor's text.

RiskRewriteRequest.description: An optional instruction to the AI for Rewrite this risk (Phase 16 D-27, Phase 15's bounds) and an optional focus: the parts of the Risk the rewrite may change (absent or null: every part). A focus, when given, names one to three distinct parts.

RiskProposalJob.description: A risk AI proposal job (Phase 16 D-26), as a human Security Analyst reads it. Jobs are process-local. riskId is the rewritten Risk, null for Suggest more risks. initiatedBy names who started the job or its latest retry; canRetry is whether this viewer may retry it now.

failureAttachments.description: For a CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE failure with files included in the AI inputs: those files in upload order by their current names. Absent otherwise.

RiskAiProposals.description: Phase 16 D-41: a risk assessment's AI proposals. openCount and openByRisk are derived from the folded item states on read; lastAskedAt is the latest completed risk proposal run's completion time. items lists the open items, grouped by run newest first, then the 50 most recently decided. jobs lists the active job per target and the latest failed job of a target with none active, while this process retains it.

editable.description: Whether the assessment passes the editable guard for the viewer now (Phase 16 D-22).

RiskAiAction.description: Whether the viewer may take a risk AI action now. Asking (suggest, rewrite) needs the editable guard, the run cap and the AI data policy; deciding needs only the guard.

reason.description: Why the act is not allowed now: ASSESSMENT_NOT_MUTABLE, AI_PROPOSAL_RUN_LIMIT or an AI data policy reason, or null when it is allowed.

RiskAiOpenByRisk.description: How many open proposed changes one Risk has.

RiskAiRunFacts.description: One completed risk proposal run: who asked, when, with which provider and instruction (and a rewrite's focus and Risk), its outcome, its item counts and its adjustments by code.

RiskAiSimilarity.description: The closest stored record a suggested risk resembles (Phase 16 D-32): an active or withdrawn Risk by its id and number, or a rejected or open earlier suggestion by its run and item key, with the similarity score.

RiskAiDecisionFacts.description: How a closed item was decided: the last decision event's action, who (null for the system or a person who cannot be read), when, a rejection's reason and a supersession's or lapse's cause.

RiskAiProposalItem.description: One proposed item: a suggested risk (kind risk, keyed s-1 to s-8) or one unit of a rewrite (kind change, keyed by its unit). state is folded from the item's decision events. stale is set for an open change only: whether the Risk no longer holds the values the change was proposed against (or is withdrawn). acceptBlocked says whether a proposed Accept would be refused now (Phase 16 D-38).

anyOf.description: Field values by AI-writable Risk field name, as the analyst reads them: text as stored, a Risk Type, system or asset by its record's name (No longer available when the record is gone), null for no value.

proposed.description: Field values by AI-writable Risk field name, as the analyst reads them: text as stored, a Risk Type, system or asset by its record's name (No longer available when the record is gone), null for no value.

RiskCurationReasonRequest.description: A withdrawal or reinstatement with a typed reason. A typed reason never marks an Undo, whatever its words.

riskIds.description: 1 to 200 unique Risk documentIds, every one of the path's assessment; a repeated id is refused, never merged.

RiskCurationUndoRequest.description: The Undo of the previous withdrawal or reinstatement (D-11): on reinstatements the server records the fixed reason `Withdrawal undone`; on withdrawals it restores the reason the Risk held before its reinstatement. The history row records `undo: true`. An Undo reverses only the acting analyst's own latest act on each Risk: on reinstatements the Risk's current withdrawal must be theirs and its most recent history row; on withdrawals its most recent history row must be their reinstatement. Otherwise the whole batch is 409 RISK_CURATION_UNDO_UNAVAILABLE and nothing is written.

riskIds.description: 1 to 200 unique Risk documentIds, every one of the path's assessment; a repeated id is refused, never merged.

RiskCurationRequest.description: Exactly one of a reason or `undo: true`. An Undo reverses only the acting analyst's own latest act on each Risk (409 RISK_CURATION_UNDO_UNAVAILABLE otherwise).

applied.description: The Risks the operation changed, each with one history row.

unchanged.description: The Risks already in the requested state, left as they were with no history row.

ScimReplaceUser.description: PUT replaces asserted source attributes under the shared user lock; omitted attributes keep current values, including active, emails, name parts and Enterprise fields. Explicit null clears optional fields. An asserted source key remains immutable. A manual candidate can be claimed only with an asserted externalId or Enterprise employeeNumber after upstream operator-confirmed correlation; knowing an id is not claim confirmation. Protected, foreign, service and tombstoned records remain hidden. No restoration, unclaim or Role writes.

externalId.description: Exact immutable source key; absent for manual correlation candidates.

ScimUser.description: Public allowlist only, without persistence relations, credentials, invented timestamps or ETag/version. Unassigned optional values are omitted.

ScimPatchRequest.description: Atomic ordered add/replace/remove against the frozen public projection inside the shared user lock; at most 100 operations and 1 MiB. Paths cover supported source attributes and selected-email equality only, never private fields or Roles. primary accepts boolean or true/false string. Added primary replaces the stored email; validated non-primary additions are not stored. emails[value eq "address"] removal of a missing address is a no-op; removing the stored address requires a new primary in the same batch. Unknown paths fail invalidPath, unmatched selection noTarget, immutable/required removal mutability; any failure rolls back the batch.

ScimEmptyGroupList.description: Groups are not supported. Always totalResults=0, startIndex=1, itemsPerPage=0, Resources=[].

externalId.description: Exact immutable source key; absent for manual correlation candidates.

ScimProjectedUser.description: Read projection; schemas and id are always retained, with other fields selected by attributes/excludedAttributes.

analyst.description: The IdamBox User documentId of the analyst who is to hold the request, or null to return it to the queue.

reason.description: Optional plain text recorded with the change, trimmed; control characters other than the newline are refused.

AssessmentRequestAssignmentAction.description: An assignment change the viewing analyst may make now. Empty for the request's own Requestor, for anyone who is not a human Security Analyst and on a draft; a released request offers no unassign.

AssessmentRequestAssignment.description: A request's assignment as an analyst sees it. People are a documentId and a display name only. history is newest first, or null when the stored history cannot be read. viewer is the analyst reading it, whom a pick-up or an assign-to-me sends as the analyst.

AssessmentRequestRequestorAssignment.description: A request's assignment as the Requestor sees it: the assignee's display name, or null when nobody holds the request.

AssignableAnalystListResponse.description: The Security Analysts who may hold a request, by documentId and display name only, ordered by display name.

RequestNotePart.description: The author's part on the request: the request's requestor (whatever role they hold), or a Security Analyst.

RequestNote.description: One note on an assessment request. The author is a documentId and a display name only, or null when the author can no longer be read.

sequence.description: 1, 2, 3 and so on per request, assigned by the server: the thread's order and the unread rule's key.

body.description: Plain text; never HTML or Markdown.

changesAiInputs.description: Served to a human Security Analyst only: whether the note is marked as changing the AI inputs.

accepting.description: Whether the request takes a new note now.

closedReason.description: Why the request takes no new note, or null while it does.

canMarkAiInputs.description: Whether the caller may mark a note as changing the AI inputs: a human Security Analyst who did not raise the request, while the request takes notes.

body.description: Plain text, trimmed, with CRLF and CR normalised to LF; 1 to 5,000 characters after trimming, no control character other than tab and newline.

changesAiInputs.description: A human Security Analyst who did not raise the request may mark the note as changing the AI inputs (off when absent). A Requestor's create carrying it is refused with 400, and a Security Analyst's on a request they raised with 403 OWN_REQUEST.

throughNoteId.description: The documentId of the note on this request through which the caller has read the thread.

changesAiInputs.description: Whether the note changes what the AI should use.

RequestNotesSummary.description: A request's notes as one viewer reads them (Phase 13 D-24, D-25): unread counts the notes written in the other part, by someone else, above the viewer's read state.

closedReason.description: Why the request takes no new note, or null while it does.

RequestAttachmentType.description: The type the content check confirmed. A .jpg and a .jpeg file are both jpeg.

RequestAttachmentState.description: available: clean and downloadable; pending: waiting for the malware check, in quarantine; blocked: the malware check found malware after upload, and the bytes are gone; removed: removed by a reader, kept on the record; unavailable: the stored bytes are gone.

RequestAttachmentPart.description: The uploader's part on the request: the request's requestor (whatever role they hold), or a Security Analyst.

RequestAttachmentActions.description: What the caller may do with the file now, as the server decides it.

RequestAttachment.description: One file on an assessment request. People are a documentId and a display name only, or null when they can no longer be read. ai is served to a human Security Analyst only; a Requestor's file carries no AI key.

fileName.description: The sanitised original name; plain text, displayed escaped.

uploadedAt.description: The server's time of the upload.

anyOf.description: The caller's note the file was posted with after submission.

detection.description: The malware check's detection name, served for a blocked file only, under the same pattern as the 422's details.detection; null when the recorded name does not match it.

RequestAttachmentAddFacts.description: Whether, and how, the caller may add a file to the request now.

refusal.description: Why the caller may not add a file now, or null while they may.

window.description: intake: a draft, its requestor adds with no note; after-submission: from submission until release or closure, each file with the caller's own note; closed: released or closed, read-only.

needsNote.description: Whether a file must be posted with the caller's own note.

remaining.description: How many more files the request takes before either limit.

activeCount.description: The files available or waiting for the malware check, not removed.

storedCount.description: Every file of the request, removed and blocked ones included.

total.description: The files not removed: the main list's count.

removed.description: The files removed from the request, listed in its removed group.

noteId.description: After submission: the caller's own note on this request, posted within the last 60 minutes.

RequestAttachmentSummary.description: A request's files as one viewer may act on them, on the request read (Phase 14 D-04 item 7): the count of files not removed and the add facts of RequestAttachmentAddFacts.

count.description: The files not removed: the main list's count.

refusal.description: Why the caller may not add a file now, or null while they may.

window.description: intake: a draft, its requestor adds with no note; after-submission: from submission until release or closure, each file with the caller's own note; closed: released or closed, read-only.

needsNote.description: Whether a file must be posted with the caller's own note.

remaining.description: How many more files the request takes before either limit.

activeCount.description: The files available or waiting for the malware check, not removed.

storedCount.description: Every file of the request, removed and blocked ones included.

RequestAttachmentRemovalRequest.description: Remove a file softly, or restore it. The only key the removal accepts.

removed.description: true removes the file; false restores it.

RequestAttachmentAiInputRequest.description: Include a file's text in what the AI may read, or exclude it. The only key the AI inclusion accepts.

included.description: true includes the file's text in what the AI may read; false excludes it and deletes the stored text.

RequestAttachmentAiFacts.description: The size of an included file's stored text: the characters the file has, the characters kept (at most 20,000), and whether the text was cut. Truncation is never silent.

RequestAttachmentAi.description: A file's AI inclusion, for a human Security Analyst only (D-28, D-30).

included.description: Whether the file's text is in what the AI may read. Off by default.

facts.description: The stored text's size while the file is included; null otherwise.

unavailableReason.description: Why the file's text cannot be included whoever asks: an image carries no text the AI can read, and a file waiting for its malware check is never read. null otherwise.

canChange.description: Whether this viewer may change the file's inclusion now, as the server decides it.

RequestAttachmentAiPolicy.description: Whether this human Security Analyst may include files in the AI inputs on this request now, and why not (D-28, D-30). Served to a human Security Analyst only; a Requestor's list carries no AI policy.

canChange.description: Whether a clean text-bearing file can be included now. Excluding an included file stays allowed while the request takes changes.

refusal.description: Why no file can be included now: the analyst raised the request (OWN_REQUEST, G-1), the request is a draft or released, or the request's AI data policy refuses. null while files can be included.

classification.description: The request's information classification, which governs what may be included (Phase 12 D-26).

ceiling.description: The highest classification the AI provider is approved for, or null when none is configured.

data.description: The stored text an included file sends to the AI, exactly as it would be sent, with its facts.

text.description: Untrusted text extracted from the file; display it as plain text.

available.description: The characters the file has after normalisation.

kept.description: The characters stored and sent: the first kept of available.

extractor.description: The extractor's version, so a change of extractor is visible in the facts it produced.

QuestionnaireGovernanceEvent.description: A stored governance event as a governance result serves it. Phase 15 (D-26): the ai-proposal and question-restored kinds and the AI keys (runId, itemKey, aiEdited, aiUndo, scope, instruction, instructionSource, providerName, providerVersion, itemCount) appear in the analyst projection only; the Requestor projection never carries an AI kind or key.

runId.description: The AI run's documentId: on ai-proposal, and on a question change a confirmation or its Undo wrote.

itemKey.description: The proposal item a confirmation or its Undo applied, with runId.

aiEdited.description: The analyst edited the proposal before confirming it, with runId and itemKey.

aiUndo.description: The event reverses a confirmed AI proposal.

scope.description: On ai-proposal: proposals for the questionnaire, or a plain-language rewrite of one question (named by questionKey and questionText).

instruction.description: The analyst's instruction to the AI, on ai-proposal and regenerated.

instructionSource.description: Written in place of an instruction when none was given: on ai-proposal exactly one of instruction and instructionSource is present; regenerated carries only default-task.

providerVersion.description: On ai-proposal: the run's provider version (the model).

itemCount.description: On ai-proposal: the proposals the run kept.

analystChangesSinceGeneration.description: Analyst reads only: question additions, edits and removals recorded at or after the questionnaire's latest generation, which replacing it would discard. Requestor reads omit it.

actor.description: The viewer the sentence is written for.

holder.description: Who holds the work at this lifecycle step, the same for every viewer: the Requestor at draft and questionnaire-released, nobody once the assessment is released, otherwise the Security Analyst. A client links the summary only when holder equals actor and href is present.

AiProposalDecision.description: One review decision on the AI proposals of the assessment details or of one Risk. A field decision leaves out `suggestion`: `accept` confirms the named `fields`, or, without `fields`, every field still proposed, so sent again once none is left it changes nothing; `restore` returns the named `fields` to proposed and must name them, so a field `restore` without `fields` is refused as invalid (400); `dismiss` applies only to a suggestion. A suggestion decision names one Risk's `suggestion` and leaves out `fields`.

AiProposalRunDecision.description: Phase 16 D-39: one human decision on a risk AI proposal item of a completed `risk-suggestions` or `risk-rewrite` run of this assessment. `accept` adds a suggested risk ("Add to assessment") or confirms one change; `reject` records the decision with an optional reason and changes nothing; `restore` undoes a rejection, or a confirmed change while the risk still holds what it confirmed (otherwise 409 AI_PROPOSAL_UNDO_UNAVAILABLE). An added risk has no undo. A run of another assessment refuses the whole batch with 404, and an item the run does not hold is a 400. `reject` and `reason` belong to this entry alone, and `dismiss` only to a suggested control.

reason.description: The one rule that refused the operation: a workflow conflict (409), an identity-relative refusal (403: OWN_REQUEST, a request the caller raised; NOT_UPLOADER and NOT_REMOVER for a file), or a request attachment refusal (400 ATTACHMENT_EMPTY; 413 ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE; 415 ATTACHMENT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED, ATTACHMENT_CONTENT_MISMATCH, ATTACHMENT_MACRO_ENABLED, ATTACHMENT_ENCRYPTED, ATTACHMENT_LEGACY_OFFICE, ATTACHMENT_UNSUPPORTED_STRUCTURE (a ZIP-based file packaged in a way CSRM will not read) and ATTACHMENT_ACTIVE_CONTENT (an Office file carrying active content beyond macros); 422 ATTACHMENT_MALWARE_FOUND; 503 ATTACHMENT_BUSY, retryable (the file checks are busy, so nothing was done); 400 INSTRUCTION_TOO_LONG, INSTRUCTION_CHARACTERS_NOT_ALLOWED and INSTRUCTION_REPEATS_REQUESTOR_TEXT (an instruction to the AI that is too long, holds characters it may not, or repeats the Requestor's text); 409 for the others, among them Phase 16's risk curation refusals RISK_WITHDRAWN (the Risk is withdrawn, so it is read-only until reinstated), RISK_NOT_WITHDRAWN (every Risk named for reinstatement is already active), AI_ACCEPT_NOT_PERMITTED (confirming an AI-proposed Accept would leave the residual rating High or Critical) and REQUEST_HAS_ASSESSMENT (a request that holds a risk assessment is never deleted), and RISK_CURATION_UNDO_UNAVAILABLE (an Undo of a withdrawal or reinstatement that is no longer the acting analyst's own latest act on a named Risk); and Phase 19's 422 EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT (the export would hold more rows than the cap; served with details.rowCount and details.rowCap), 409 ASSESSMENT_NOT_RELEASED (an unreleased risk assessment the caller can read cannot be exported), 422 EXPORT_CELL_TOO_LONG (an xlsx export would hold a text cell longer than Excel's 32,767-character cell limit; served with details.column and details.cellLimit; the CSV holds the value whole), the import file refusals, served with details.found where it applies (415 IMPORT_FILE_TYPE, not a CSV or .xlsx file; 413 IMPORT_FILE_TOO_LARGE, more than 5 MB; 422 IMPORT_TOO_MANY_ROWS, more than 5,000 rows; 422 IMPORT_ENCODING_WINDOWS_1252, IMPORT_ENCODING_UTF16 and IMPORT_ENCODING_UNKNOWN, a file that is not UTF-8 text; 422 IMPORT_DELIMITER, columns separated by semicolons or tabs; 422 IMPORT_LEGACY_XLS, IMPORT_MACRO_WORKBOOK, IMPORT_ENCRYPTED_WORKBOOK and IMPORT_WORKBOOK_TOO_LARGE, a workbook CSRM will not open; 422 IMPORT_NO_HEADER, IMPORT_NO_ROWS, IMPORT_DUPLICATE_HEADER and IMPORT_MISSING_COLUMN, a header row CSRM cannot use), and the import commit's 409 IMPORT_DECISION_MISSING (a row matched by similar name has no decision) and 409 IMPORT_REVIEW_EXPIRED (the reviewed preview has expired or is unknown), and 422 IMPORT_CSV_MALFORMED (a CSV file the parser cannot read: an unclosed quote, an invalid closing quote, or a row with a different number of columns from the header; served with details.found.line when the parser reports the line)). Closed list; a client that does not know a value falls back to its generic message.

detection.description: The scanner's name for the malware it found. Served only beside ATTACHMENT_MALWARE_FOUND (422), and shown to the person as data.

rowCount.description: The number of rows the refused export would hold. Served only beside EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT (422).

rowCap.description: The most rows one export may hold. Served only beside EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT (422).

column.description: The key of the first column whose text cell is longer than Excel allows, from the export's closed column vocabulary; never a value. Served only beside EXPORT_CELL_TOO_LONG (422).

cellLimit.description: The most characters one xlsx text cell may hold, the neutraliser's mark included (Excel's limit). Served only beside EXPORT_CELL_TOO_LONG (422).

found.description: What a refused import file was found to hold, so the refusal can name the fix. Served only beside an IMPORT_ reason; never holds a cell value.

headers.description: The file's own column headers the refusal concerns, as typed, with control characters removed.

labels.description: The display labels of the columns the refusal concerns.

delimiter.description: The separator the header line uses in place of a comma.

rows.description: The data rows the file holds.

bytes.description: The size of the file in bytes.

line.description: The 1-based source line on which the CSV parser failed. Served only beside IMPORT_CSV_MALFORMED, and only when the parser reports one; never the line's content.

requestStatus.description: Every status a review queue reads: the action queues return submitted, questionnaire-in-progress, risk-assessment-drafted and under-review requests, the released queue returns approved and closed requests, and no queue returns a draft.

requestorName.description: The requestor's display name, or null when the request records no requestor. No other requestor field is served.

businessCriticality.description: The business criticality the Requestor recorded: a business attribute, not a risk rating.

daysSinceSubmission.description: Whole UTC calendar days from the submission date to the server's UTC today, never negative; null when the request has no submission date.

assignee.description: The Security Analyst who holds the request, as a documentId and a display name only, or null when nobody has picked it up (D-13).

pickUp.description: Whether the viewer may pick the request up, decided by the assignment operation's own rules (D-13, D-16): allowed for a human Security Analyst on an unassigned request they did not raise; own-request when the viewer raised it, so it is never theirs to pick up (D-07); not-offered otherwise (held by someone, or a viewer who is not a human Security Analyst). The assignment operation decides again on every change.

unreadNotes.description: How many of the request's notes are new to the viewer (D-24): written in the other part, not by the viewer, and after the viewer's read state. 0 for a viewer who may not use the request's notes.

AssessmentRequestQueueMeta.description: The queue read's pagination, and its viewer: the analyst reading it, as a documentId and a display name, whom the queue's Pick up sends as the analyst (13-12).

canRetry.description: Whether the job failed and the viewing analyst may retry it (D-18). Any human Security Analyst who may read the request may retry a failed job.

initiatedBy.description: The analyst who started the job, or who started its latest retry; null when that person can no longer be read (D-18).

initiatedByViewer.description: Whether the viewing analyst started the job or its latest retry (D-18).

canRetry.description: Whether the job failed and the viewing analyst may retry it (D-18). Any human Security Analyst who may read the request may retry a failed job.

initiatedBy.description: The analyst who started the job, or who started its latest retry; null when that person can no longer be read (D-18).

initiatedByViewer.description: Whether the viewing analyst started the job or its latest retry (D-18).

initiatedBy.description: The analyst who started the job, or who started its latest retry; null when that person can no longer be read (D-18).

initiatedByViewer.description: Whether the viewing analyst started the job or its latest retry (D-18).

failureAttachments.description: Phase 14 D-33: for a CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE failure with files included in the AI inputs, those files in upload order, by their current names; absent otherwise.

canRetry.description: Whether the job failed and the viewing analyst may retry it (D-18). Any human Security Analyst who may read the request may retry a failed job.

initiatedBy.description: The analyst who started the job, or who started its latest retry; null when that person can no longer be read (D-18).

initiatedByViewer.description: Whether the viewing analyst started the job or its latest retry (D-18).

AiRun.description: What an AI run used and how it ended (Phase 12 D-25). Never the proposal and never Requestor free text. Phase 15 adds the questionnaire-proposals and question-rewrite operations; Phase 16 adds risk-suggestions ("Suggest more risks") and risk-rewrite ("Rewrite this risk", whose targets.risk is the rewritten Risk). instruction is the exact validated instruction a Security Analyst gave, or null (a rewrite on CSRM's plain-language preset stores none).

AiRunContextSummary.description: The closed summary of the context an AI run used. The stored summary holds no Requestor, note or file free text (a file is named by its documentId and digest); on the read, each file's current name is resolved from its attachment record. digest is sha256 over the exact prompt. Version 2 (Phase 13) adds the notes the run used; a version 1 summary, written before notes reached the context, is served with an empty notes section. Version 3 (Phase 14) adds the files the run used; a version 1 or 2 summary, written before files reached the context, is served with an empty attachments section. Version 4 (Phase 15) adds questionnaire, what a questionnaire proposal or rewrite run was shown of the questionnaire (null for questionnaire generation and the draft), and instruction, what steered the run by its source only (null for the draft); a version 1 to 3 summary is served with both null. Version 5 (Phase 16) adds riskProposals, what a risk-suggestions or risk-rewrite run listed, as counts and closed values only (null for every other operation); a version 1 to 4 summary is served with it null. None holds the instruction's text, a Risk's text or any Requestor text.

AiRunContextAttachments.description: The request files an AI run used (Phase 14 D-35): those a Security Analyst included in the AI inputs when its context was built, in upload order, at most 20. Each is named by its documentId and digest, never its text; its name is resolved when the run is read. bound is the characters of file text one run of the operation may send (30,000 for questionnaire generation, questionnaire proposals and a question rewrite, 60,000 for an assessment draft and the two risk proposal operations).

AiRunContextQuestionnaire.description: What a questionnaire proposal or rewrite run was shown of the questionnaire (Phase 15 D-14), as counts and closed values only. scope is questionnaire for questionnaire proposals and question for a rewrite. questionsOffered counts the questions sent and answered those answered, which the AI treats as fixed. answerContent is included only when every active, visible question held a submitted answer; a rewrite sends no answers. The open, rejected and removed items listed are bounded; the rejected items are the most recent, and rejectedItemsTotal counts them all.

AiRunContextRiskProposals.description: What a risk proposal run listed (Phase 16 D-25, D-31, D-35), as counts and closed values only: never a Risk's text, a reason or the instruction's text. scope is assessment for risk-suggestions and risk for risk-rewrite. risksListed counts the active Risks listed (already in the assessment; for a rewrite, the assessment's other active Risks); withdrawnListed, rejectedListed and openListed count the withdrawn Risks and the rejected and open suggestions listed (zero for a rewrite). Together they are at most 200. controlsListed counts the rewritten Risk's control implementations and focus is the rewrite's focus (null for every part); both are null for risk-suggestions.

AiRunContextInstruction.description: What steered an AI run (Phase 15 D-17), by its source only, never its text: analyst (the run's instruction), plain-language-preset (CSRM's own rewrite request) or default-task (no instruction; the operation's own task).

AiRunContextAttachment.description: One file an AI run used: its documentId, digest, type, the part that uploaded it, the characters sent and available and whether the text sent was truncated; never its text. fileName, requestId and removed are what the attachment record says when the run is read: its current name and request (null when the record no longer exists) and whether it has been removed since.

QuestionnaireAiProposals.description: Phase 15 D-03 item 4: the questionnaire's open AI proposal items, newest run first, then the 50 most recently decided items; the runs' facts; the active jobs; the answered (fixed) questions in analyst review and on a submitted questionnaire (null otherwise); and what the viewing analyst may do now.

QuestionnaireAiProposalItem.description: One proposed addition, change or removal. `stale` is null while the Requestor is answering and for a decided item.

QuestionnaireAiRunFacts.description: One completed proposal or rewrite run: who asked, when, the provider, the instruction or what steered it, and what the adapter left out (by code and count).

reason.description: Why the act is not allowed now: a closed conflict reason, or null when it is allowed.

QuestionnaireProposalJob.description: A questionnaire AI proposal or question rewrite job (Phase 15 D-16), as a human Security Analyst reads it. Jobs are process-local.

failureAttachments.description: For a CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE failure with files included in the AI inputs: those files in upload order by their current names. Absent otherwise.

action.description: accept is shown as Confirm; restore undoes a confirmation or a rejection.

edits.description: Edit, then confirm: the fields the analyst changed before confirming, each held to the manual question edit's rule. `section` applies to an addition only.

QuestionnaireAiInstructionRequest.description: An optional instruction to the AI (Phase 15 D-17 to D-19): at most 500 characters, no control or bidirectional characters, and not a repeat of the Requestor's text.

GenerationJobFailureAttachment.description: A file a CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE generation failure counted (Phase 14 D-33): one included in the AI inputs when the context was refused, by its documentId and its current name (null when the record no longer exists), so the analyst can exclude it.

AiRunContextNotes.description: The request notes an AI run used: those marked as changing the AI inputs when its context was built, at most 50. Each is named without its text.

AiRunContextNote.description: One note an AI run used, by its documentId, part, sequence, posting time and length in characters; never its text.

AiGenerationFacts.description: Who generated a record through an AI provider, when, with which provider, and the run behind the latest generation (null for one generated before run records existed). Analyst reads only.

aiInputsChanged.description: Phase 13 D-29 and Phase 14 D-36: the notes whose AI-input mark changed since this generation (marked since, or included and since unmarked) and the files whose inclusion changed (included, excluded or removed since), for a human Security Analyst; null when nothing changed, the record has no baseline, or the viewer is not a human Security Analyst.

openProposals.description: Questionnaire reads only (Phase 15 D-28, D-32): how many AI proposal items on the questionnaire wait for an analyst's decision, for a human Security Analyst who did not raise the request; null for any other analyst. Absent from an assessment's generation facts.

AiInputsChanged.description: Phase 13 D-29 and Phase 14 D-36: AI inputs changed since the last generation. The notes whose current AI-input mark differs from what the record's baseline (the completed context-wide run its generation.runId names, or the generation date of a record generated before run records existed) included, in sequence order, and the files whose current inclusion in the AI inputs differs from the same baseline's, in upload order; never their text. count is the notes changed plus the files changed. The signal is served when either list has an item, so one list may be empty but never both. Advisory and analyst-only.

AiInputsChangedNote.description: One note whose AI-input mark changed since the baseline: marked (marked now, not used then) or unmarked (used then, no longer marked). Named by documentId, part, sequence and posting time only.

AiInputsChangedFile.description: Phase 14 D-36: one file whose inclusion in the AI inputs changed since the baseline: included (in the inputs now, not used then), excluded (used then, excluded since or no longer scanned clean) or removed (used then, removed since). Named by documentId and current name only; never its text or digest.

RequestAiInputs.description: Phase 13 D-29 and Phase 14 D-36: the AI-inputs signal (notes and files) for each target of a request; a target is null when it does not exist, has no baseline, or nothing changed.

AiSourceCitation.description: A context source an AI-written statement cites, resolved from the proposing run's catalogue. A source the catalogue no longer holds reads Source no longer available.

AiFieldReview.description: One AI-written field's review state; sources are given only for statement fields.

AiSuggestionReview.description: A suggested mitigation control and its review state; present means the control already mitigates the risk.

RiskAiProvenance.description: A risk's AI review state for the analyst (Phase 12 D-12, D-14, D-21).

outstanding.description: How many AI-written fields are still proposed.

AssessmentAiProvenance.description: The assessment's own AI review state for the analyst.

generatedBy.description: The Security Analyst who initiated the draft, on the analyst list. Null on the Requestor's own list (GET /v1/my_risk_assessments): who generated a draft is analyst-only (D-23).

requestTitle.description: The title of the assessment's Assessment Request, or null when the assessment records no request or the title is blank.

riskCount.description: How many Risks the assessment holds.

highestResidualRating.description: The highest residual rating, Low to Critical, among the assessment's Risks. A Risk with no residual rating, or one outside that scale, is counted in riskCount but never rates; null when no Risk is rated.

MyRequestStatusSummary.description: The signed-in actor's own assessment requests counted by requestStatus, one key per status. total is the sum of the seven status counts. byHolder counts the same requests by who holds them, and its three counts also sum to total. withUnreadNotes counts the requests with at least one note new to the caller as their Requestor, equal to the total of GET /v1/my_requests?notes=unread.

withUnreadNotes.description: The caller's own requests with at least one note new to them as the Requestor (D-24).

MyRequestHolderCounts.description: The signed-in actor's own assessment requests counted by holder, with the same definition as GET /v1/my_requests?holder=: requestor (waiting on the caller as its Requestor), analyst (with the Security Analyst) and none (released or closed).

MyRequestItem.description: One of the signed-in actor's own assessment requests, read from the Requestor's side. It carries no Risk Assessment field: an unreleased assessment's identity is never disclosed.

daysSinceSubmission.description: Whole UTC calendar days from the submission date to the server's UTC today, never negative; null when the request has no submission date.

holder.description: Who holds the request at its lifecycle stage, equal to the lifecycle next action's holder: the Requestor at draft and questionnaire-released, nobody once the assessment is released or the request is closed, otherwise the Security Analyst.

anyOf.description: The Requestor-side next step sentence. href is present only when the Requestor holds the step and may open its record.
Set for a draft the Security Analyst returned: the recorded reason and when it was returned.
Set once the questionnaire is released to the Requestor: how many of its active questions hold an answer, out of how many.

assignee.description: The Security Analyst who holds the request, by display name alone, or null when nobody has picked it up (D-17).

unreadNotes.description: How many of the request's notes are new to the caller as its Requestor (D-24): written by a Security Analyst, not by the caller, and after the caller's read state.

MyRequestAssignee.description: The Security Analyst who holds one of the caller's requests, as the Requestor sees them: the display name and nothing more (D-17).

CurrentUserAccess.description: The signed-in IdamBox User's effective access. functions are the menu Functions (those with a menuPath) held through any effective Role, sorted by menuPath; operations are the granted FunctionApi urls (METHOD:/api/v1/...), sorted.

DashboardSummary.description: The analyst dashboard's figures on the server's UTC calendar date, today. dueSoonWindowDays is the due-soon window every treatment due state and treatment count uses.

DashboardReviewQueue.description: Work waiting in each analyst review list, each count equal to that list's total. requiresAttention, awaitingRequestor and generationInProgress are the team's Assessment Request queues. questionnairesReadyForReview counts the questionnaires whose answers are submitted. assessmentsDraft and assessmentsInReview count Risk Assessments by status. mine counts the requests the viewer holds (Phase 13 D-15). unassigned counts the requests that require attention and that nobody holds, equal to the requires-attention queue filtered by assignee=unassigned.

DashboardReviewQueueMine.description: The viewer's own Assessment Request counts (Phase 13 D-15), the viewer being the IdamBox User the policy resolved. requiresAttention, awaitingRequestor and generationInProgress each equal that queue filtered by assignee=me; withUnreadNotes equals the open queue filtered by assignee=me and notes=unread.

DashboardRiskExposure.description: Open Risks by residual rating, in the Risk Register's two stages, never added together. released counts the open Risks whose risk assessment is released (approved, with an approval date and an approver); releasedAccepted counts those among them whose treatment action is Accept; underAssessment counts the open Risks whose risk assessment is a draft or in review, with no release facts. A draft's Accept never counts as accepted. Each count equals the Risk Register filtered by that residual rating, state=open and stage=released (with treatmentAction=Accept) or stage=under-assessment.

DashboardHighCriticalRisks.description: Released open Risks rated High or Critical after treatment, where the risk assessment is released (approved, with an approval date and an approver); a Risk under assessment is never listed. Critical first, then target date ascending with undated Risks last, then Risk number. total counts every such Risk, equal to the Risk Register filtered by residualRating=Critical and by residualRating=High, each with state=open and stage=released, and truncated says rows is capped.

DashboardRiskRow.description: One released open High or Critical residual Risk. treatmentDueState is derived by the server on its UTC calendar date.

DashboardTreatmentsDue.description: Open Risk treatments past their target date or due within the window, over the risk-treatment-overdue and risk-treatment-due-soon alert predicates: overdue and dueSoon each equal the total of that kind's alert list, and total equals the list of both kinds.

DashboardRecentActivity.description: The most recent workflow events in the analyst review scope, newest first. truncated says there are more events than rows shows.

ActivityKind.description: The closed set of workflow events. A generated draft is advisory and names no one; a release names the Security Analyst who released it.

ActivityItem.description: One workflow event. recordType names the kind of record the event is about and documentId identifies it. identifier is its request, questionnaire or assessment number, and is null for a questionnaire that has no number. title is the request title, the questionnaire title, or the owning request's title for an assessment. actorDisplayName is the display name of the identity the event names, and is null when the event names no one or none is recorded. occurredAt is the instant the event was recorded.

AlertKind.description: The closed set of derived alert conditions.

AlertUrgency.description: How soon an alert needs action. It is never a Risk rating.

AlertLinkType.description: The record an alert links to. A Control Implementation alert links to its parent Risk.

AlertSource.description: The record whose facts raise the alert. identifier is the Risk number for Risk and Control Implementation sources, the request number for requests and the assessment number for assessments. released is true when that work's assessment is released and read-only.

AlertItem.description: One derived alert. id is the kind and the source documentId joined by a colon. dayOffset counts whole UTC days from the server's today to the governing date, negative once it has passed, and is null without a date. residualRating is the (parent) Risk's residual rating, null for requests and assessments.

AlertListMeta.description: today is the UTC calendar date the alerts were derived on. dueSoonWindowDays is the window, in days from today inclusive, that counts as due soon.

AlertSummary.description: Every current alert counted by kind and by urgency over the same predicate as GET /v1/alerts. total is the number of alerts.

ReportKey.description: The closed set of analyst reports.

ReportDefinition.description: One analyst report as the Reports index lists it.

RatingCounts.description: Risks by rating on the closed ladder. notRated counts a Risk with no rating, or one outside the ladder. The parts add up to total.

TreatmentStatusCounts.description: Risks by the treatment status recorded on each Risk. notProvided counts a Risk with no recorded status. The parts add up to total.

ControlStatusCounts.description: Control Implementations by implementation status. notProvided counts one with no recorded status. The parts add up to total.

EffectivenessCounts.description: Control Implementations by effectiveness rating. notProvided counts one with no recorded rating. The parts add up to total.

RequestStatusCounts.description: Assessment Requests in the Security Analyst's review scope by status. A draft is outside that scope and is never counted. The parts add up to total.

ResidualByTreatmentStatus.description: Released open Risks by residual rating, each split by recorded treatment status. notRated holds the Risks with no rating on the ladder.

ExposedSystem.description: One Information System with the released open High and Critical residual Risks that impact it.

ExposedSystems.description: The Information Systems carrying the most released open High and Critical residual Risks: most Critical first, then most in total, then by name. total counts every such system and truncated says rows is capped. risksWithoutSystem counts the released open High and Critical residual Risks that impact no Information System.

TreatmentDueStateCounts.description: Open treatments that are not Complete, by due state on the server's today: overdue has a target date before today, dueWithinWindow one from today to today plus dueWindowDays inclusive, later one after that, and noTargetDate none. Each part equals the Risk Register filtered by its dueState (overdue, due-soon, later, no-target-date), and overdue and dueWithinWindow equal the risk-treatment-overdue and risk-treatment-due-soon alert lists. The parts add up to total.

MostOverdueTreatments.description: The risk-treatment-overdue alerts with the oldest target dates, oldest first. total counts every such alert and truncated says rows is capped.

ThroughputMonth.description: One UTC calendar month. monthStart is its first day, count the Risk Assessments released in it, and partial marks the current month, which is still in progress.

ThroughputReleased.description: Released Risk Assessments per month over the period, oldest month first. total is the sum of the months.

MedianDaysToRelease.description: The median days from request submission to release, rounded to one decimal, over the releases in the period whose request records a submission. value is null when there is none. The sample is capped, newest first, and truncated says so.

RiskExposureUnderAssessment.description: The open Risks whose risk assessment is a draft or in review, with no release facts, by residual rating. They are counted apart from every released section and never added to one. Each count equals the Risk Register filtered by that residual rating (none for notRated), state=open and stage=under-assessment.

RiskExposureReport.description: Released open Risks (those whose risk assessment is approved, with an approval date and an approver) by residual and by inherent rating, the accepted ones among them by residual rating, residual rating by treatment status, and the most exposed Information Systems; and, apart, the open Risks still under assessment. Each released count equals the Risk Register filtered by that rating (none for notRated), state=open and stage=released, with treatmentAction=Accept for acceptedByResidualRating; a draft's Accept never counts as accepted. today is the UTC calendar date the report was computed on.

TreatmentPerformanceReport.description: Open treatments by due state, read with the one shared due-state rule over a window of dueWindowDays (the product's due-soon window, the alerts' window), open Risks by recorded treatment status, and the most overdue treatments; every figure includes Risks under assessment as well as released ones. today is the UTC calendar date the report was computed on.

AssessmentThroughputReport.description: Risk Assessments released per UTC calendar month over the period months ending with the current month, which begins on periodStart, the median days from submission to release over the same period, and Assessment Requests by status as a current snapshot. today is the UTC calendar date the report was computed on.

ControlEffectivenessReport.description: Control Implementations on open Risks, released or under assessment, by implementation status and by effectiveness rating. today is the UTC calendar date the report was computed on.

assignment.description: Phase 13 D-16: who holds the request and whether the viewer may pick it up, on a human Security Analyst's assessment read; null on every other read, a Requestor's included.

notes.description: Phase 13 D-25: the request's notes figures for the viewer, on a human Security Analyst's assessment read; null on every other read, a Requestor's included.

files.description: Phase 14 D-27: the request's files figures, on a human Security Analyst's assessment read; null on every other read, a Requestor's included.

RiskWithdrawal.description: Why, when and by whom a Risk was withdrawn from its assessment (Phase 16 D-05, D-06). Shown to Security Analysts only.

by.description: The withdrawing analyst; null when the person can no longer be named.

aiProvenance.description: The risk's AI review state for the analyst; null when no AI proposal wrote it or its record cannot be read.

withdrawal.description: Null on an active Risk. A withdrawn Risk stays on the analyst's assessment, out of its release readiness and counts, and never reaches a Requestor.

generation.description: Null when the assessment was never generated.

released.description: Phase 19 (D-14): whether the assessment is released, decided by the one released-assessment record-read check for an analyst: approved with its complete release facts, on an approved request. The analyst page offers the export and the print report only when it is true.

aiAssisted.description: True when the assessment was drafted with an AI provider. The Requestor learns nothing else of the AI facts, including who generated the draft.

stage.description: released: the Risk's assessment carries the complete release facts. under-assessment: its assessment is a draft or in review with no release facts.

treatmentAction.description: The Risk's recorded treatment action, or null when none is recorded. Accepted is a released, open Risk whose treatment action is Accept.

accepted.description: Server-derived D-41 marker: true only for a released, open Risk whose treatment action is Accept. A Complete treatment without a closure date is still open.

TreatmentDueState.description: The server-derived treatment due state on the server's UTC calendar date. complete-or-closed: the treatment is Complete or the Risk has a closure date. no-target-date: an open treatment with no target date. overdue: the target date is before today. due-soon: the target date is today or within the next 14 days. later: the target date is further out. The stored Overdue treatment status is never read.

withdrawal.description: Null on an active Risk. Who withdrew the Risk, when and why; a withdrawn Risk is listed only under the register's withdrawn state and counts in no figure (Phase 16 D-08, D-45).

AssessmentRiskListItem.description: D-34: one Risk in an assessment's risk list, the read both actors' released views render: the statement, the affected system and asset by name, the inherent and residual likelihood, consequence and rating, the treatment action, plan and status, and the risk owner, treatment owner and target date (brief section 8). The Risk create and update responses keep RiskSummary.

controlSummary.description: D-34: the implemented control's number, name and framework, so every reader names it without the id. Null when the control lacks one of them or one falls outside its bounds.

ControlImplementationControlSummary.description: D-34: a bounded summary of the control a mitigation control implements, with the Administration control record's bounds.

RiskTypeApplicableControl.description: D-31: a control that applies to a Risk Type, summarised for the mitigation control picker with the Administration control record's bounds.

applicableControls.description: D-31: the controls that apply to this Risk Type, sorted by control number, so the control picker offers them first.

reason.description: The one rule that refused the operation: a workflow conflict (409), an identity-relative refusal (403: OWN_REQUEST, a request the caller raised; NOT_UPLOADER and NOT_REMOVER for a file), or a request attachment refusal (400 ATTACHMENT_EMPTY; 413 ATTACHMENT_TOO_LARGE; 415 ATTACHMENT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED, ATTACHMENT_CONTENT_MISMATCH, ATTACHMENT_MACRO_ENABLED, ATTACHMENT_ENCRYPTED, ATTACHMENT_LEGACY_OFFICE, ATTACHMENT_UNSUPPORTED_STRUCTURE (a ZIP-based file packaged in a way CSRM will not read) and ATTACHMENT_ACTIVE_CONTENT (an Office file carrying active content beyond macros); 422 ATTACHMENT_MALWARE_FOUND; 503 ATTACHMENT_BUSY, retryable (the file checks are busy, so nothing was done); 400 INSTRUCTION_TOO_LONG, INSTRUCTION_CHARACTERS_NOT_ALLOWED and INSTRUCTION_REPEATS_REQUESTOR_TEXT (an instruction to the AI that is too long, holds characters it may not, or repeats the Requestor's text); 409 for the others, among them Phase 16's risk curation refusals RISK_WITHDRAWN (the Risk is withdrawn, so it is read-only until reinstated), RISK_NOT_WITHDRAWN (every Risk named for reinstatement is already active), AI_ACCEPT_NOT_PERMITTED (confirming an AI-proposed Accept would leave the residual rating High or Critical) and REQUEST_HAS_ASSESSMENT (a request that holds a risk assessment is never deleted), and RISK_CURATION_UNDO_UNAVAILABLE (an Undo of a withdrawal or reinstatement that is no longer the acting analyst's own latest act on a named Risk); and Phase 19's 422 EXPORT_ROW_LIMIT (the export would hold more rows than the cap; served with details.rowCount and details.rowCap), 409 ASSESSMENT_NOT_RELEASED (an unreleased risk assessment the caller can read cannot be exported), 422 EXPORT_CELL_TOO_LONG (an xlsx export would hold a text cell longer than Excel's 32,767-character cell limit; served with details.column and details.cellLimit; the CSV holds the value whole), the import file refusals, served with details.found where it applies (415 IMPORT_FILE_TYPE, not a CSV or .xlsx file; 413 IMPORT_FILE_TOO_LARGE, more than 5 MB; 422 IMPORT_TOO_MANY_ROWS, more than 5,000 rows; 422 IMPORT_ENCODING_WINDOWS_1252, IMPORT_ENCODING_UTF16 and IMPORT_ENCODING_UNKNOWN, a file that is not UTF-8 text; 422 IMPORT_DELIMITER, columns separated by semicolons or tabs; 422 IMPORT_LEGACY_XLS, IMPORT_MACRO_WORKBOOK, IMPORT_ENCRYPTED_WORKBOOK and IMPORT_WORKBOOK_TOO_LARGE, a workbook CSRM will not open; 422 IMPORT_NO_HEADER, IMPORT_NO_ROWS, IMPORT_DUPLICATE_HEADER and IMPORT_MISSING_COLUMN, a header row CSRM cannot use), and the import commit's 409 IMPORT_DECISION_MISSING (a row matched by similar name has no decision) and 409 IMPORT_REVIEW_EXPIRED (the reviewed preview has expired or is unknown), and 422 IMPORT_CSV_MALFORMED (a CSV file the parser cannot read: an unclosed quote, an invalid closing quote, or a row with a different number of columns from the header; served with details.found.line when the parser reports the line)). Closed list; a client that does not know a value falls back to its generic message.

failureAttachments.description: Phase 14 D-33: for a CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE failure with files included in the AI inputs, those files in upload order, by their current names; absent otherwise.

canRetry.description: Whether the job failed and the viewing analyst may retry it (D-18). Any human Security Analyst who may read the request may retry a failed job.

initiatedBy.description: The analyst who started the job, or who started its latest retry; null when that person can no longer be read (D-18).

initiatedByViewer.description: Whether the viewing analyst started the job or its latest retry (D-18).

canRetry.description: Whether the job failed and the viewing analyst may retry it, the job's own canRetry (D-18). Any human Security Analyst who may read the request may retry a failed job; who started it is the job's initiatedBy and initiatedByViewer.

Whether the job failed and the viewing analyst may retry it, the job's own canRetry (D-18). Any human Security Analyst who may read the request may retry a failed job; who started it is the job's initiatedBy and initiatedByViewer.

AiPolicyStatus.description: D-29: the AI data policy the next generation for this request would apply. A refused status names its closed reason; the hub shows it in place of the action.

assignment.description: Phase 13 D-16: who holds the request and whether the viewer may pick it up, on a human Security Analyst's questionnaire read; null on every other read, a Requestor's included.

notes.description: Phase 13 D-25: the request's notes figures for the viewer, on a human Security Analyst's questionnaire read; null on every other read, a Requestor's included.

files.description: Phase 14 D-27: the request's files figures, on a human Security Analyst's questionnaire read; null on every other read, a Requestor's included.

RequestSummaryAssignment.description: Phase 13 D-16 (REQ-08 criterion 1): who holds the request, as a documentId and a display name, or null when nobody does; and whether the viewer may pick it up, by the review queue's rule (own-request: the viewer raised it).

RequestSummaryNotes.description: Phase 13 D-25: how many notes the request holds, and how many are new to the viewer, by the request read's unread rule.

RequestSummaryFiles.description: Phase 14 D-27: how many files the request holds (not removed), and how many of them are included in the AI inputs (included, scanned clean and not removed). Never a file's name, text or digest.

aiAssisted.description: True when the questionnaire was generated through an AI provider.

QuestionnaireRevisionTimelineEvent.description: An event of the revision timeline as the reader's projection serves it. Phase 15 (D-26): the ai-proposal and question-restored kinds and the AI keys (runId, itemKey, aiEdited, aiUndo, scope, instruction, instructionSource, providerName, providerVersion, itemCount) appear in the analyst projection only; the Requestor projection never carries an AI kind or key.

runId.description: The AI run's documentId: on ai-proposal, and on a question change a confirmation or its Undo wrote.

itemKey.description: The proposal item a confirmation or its Undo applied, with runId.

aiEdited.description: The analyst edited the proposal before confirming it, with runId and itemKey.

aiUndo.description: The event reverses a confirmed AI proposal.

scope.description: On ai-proposal: proposals for the questionnaire, or a plain-language rewrite of one question (named by questionKey and questionText).

AdministrationImportState.description: An import row's state. similar (Matched by similar name): the row's natural key equals a stored record's only after NFKC, lower case and collapsed whitespace; it is neither created nor updated until the commit carries a decision for it (D-30).

skipped.description: Rows matched by similar name that the Security Analyst decided to skip. A similar row decided update counts under update.

matchedName.description: The matched record's stored natural key (its name, or a Control's control number) for an update, unchanged or similar row; null otherwise.

AdministrationImportResultRow.description: documentId is returned only when state is create or update, or similar with decision update; unchanged, rejected, ambiguous and skipped similar rows have no write result. A similar row keeps its state and carries the decision it was committed with.

decision.description: The Security Analyst's decision for a similar row; present only when state is similar.

decisions.description: Optional. A JSON object of row number (a string of 1 to 5 digits) to update or skip, at most 5,000 entries. Every similar row of the reviewed preview needs one (else 409 IMPORT_DECISION_MISSING); a decision for any other row, or a malformed field, is 400.

warnings.description: The file's headers that match no import column, as typed (controls removed), in file order: ignored, and named so the person sees them (D-27).

notes.description: Informational notes, each at most once: issues-column (the error report's Issues column, ignored), read-only-columns (a reference export's read-only columns, ignored; named in readOnlyColumns) and example-row (the template's example row, skipped).

readOnlyColumns.description: The display labels of the reference export's read-only columns the file carries, ignored (D-33).

resultToken.description: An opaque token for the commit's result record, bound to the actor and collection for five minutes (D-32).

ownerName.description: The owner's display name, trimmed; null when there is no owner or the owner has no display name.
